question:
Two nuclei are studied using **atomic masses** (so electrons are already included in the given masses).

Data: mass of hydrogen atom $m_H=1.007825\,u$, mass of neutron $m_n=1.008665\,u$, and $1\,u\,c^2=931.5\,\text{MeV}$.

Nucleus 1: $^{16}\!O$ has atomic mass $M(^{16}\!O)=15.994915\,u$.
Nucleus 2: $^{12}\!C$ has atomic mass $M(^{12}\!C)=12.000000\,u$.

(a) Determine the **composition** of each nucleus (values of $Z$, $N$, and $A$).

(b) Using atomic masses, calculate the **mass defect** for each nucleus using
$\Delta m = Zm_H + (A-Z)m_n - M_{atom}$.

(c) Hence calculate the **binding energy per nucleon** for each nucleus.

(d) Evaluate which nucleus is more stable based on your result and justify clearly using the concept of $\dfrac{BE}{A}$.

options.D: $\left(\dfrac{BE}{A}\right)_{^{16}\!O}\approx 7.98\,\text{MeV},\;\left(\dfrac{BE}{A}\right)_{^{12}\!C}\approx 7.68\,\text{MeV};\;^{12}\!C\text{ is more stable because it has smaller }A$
